notable_absence.finding: Capella explicitly does NOT support a whole category of SSO flow: 'Capella supports service provider-initiated (SP-initiated) authentication only. Capella does not support identity provider-initiated (IdP-initiated) sign-in, where there's a sign-in request through the SSO page of the IdP.' A genuine documented absence of a capability, not a gap in extraction.

cross_component_finding: This page is the clearest confirmation of the hypothesis: authentication (auth:sso, auth:mfa - 'how you prove who you are') and authorization (capella-role:* - 'what you're allowed to do') are kept as genuinely separate axes throughout, and the only place they touch is gating: Organization Owner (a capella-role) is required to CONFIGURE the auth mechanism (realms, teams), but the auth mechanism itself never grants or IS a role - team-to-permission-set mapping is described in its own vocabulary ('permission sets'), which this page never explicitly equates to capella-role:*, rbac-role:role, or any project-role concept. I deliberately minted auth:permission-set as an unresolved placeholder rather than guessing which existing role family it maps to - that ambiguity itself is worth flagging to the reconciler. Secondary finding: 'MFA' is used for two distinct things on this page - Capella's own built-in MFA (auth:mfa) and 'their own built-in multi-factor authentication (MFA)' provided by every supported IdP - a smaller-scale naming collision in the same shape as the batch's known role-name collisions, though not asked about explicitly it's worth flagging alongside them.
